# Current and temperature of the motor phase paths (generated by report.py)

DC current in the six phase pours (J1 to shunt, shunt to J2) on the routed copper and steady temperature of the whole board, 35 A rms in each of the three phases, still air at 25 C, board horizontal (power_paths.py; solvers checked by validate_solver.py). The RMS current sets the heat whatever the waveform.

## Current paths at 35 A rms

| Phase | R J1 to shunt | R shunt to J2 | Drop over the copper | Copper loss | Shunt loss | Densest current (outside the vias) | Most current in one via |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| U (R1) | 0.104 mOhm | 0.105 mOhm | 7.3 mV | 0.26 W | 1.22 W | 59 A/mm2 | 0.01 A |
| V (R4) | 0.089 mOhm | 0.089 mOhm | 6.2 mV | 0.22 W | 1.22 W | 49 A/mm2 | 0.02 A |
| W (R7) | 0.109 mOhm | 0.108 mOhm | 7.6 mV | 0.27 W | 1.23 W | 59 A/mm2 | 0.02 A |

The four layers carry the same pour, so the current splits by copper thickness: L1 33 %, L2 17 %, L3 17 %, L6 33 %, and the vias carry almost nothing; the pins of J1, J2 and the shunts tie the layers together. The copper adds 20 % to the shunt heat: the shunts (1.22 W each) and, if present, the connector contacts dominate.

## Temperatures at 35 A rms

| | Copper and shunts | Plus MR60PW contacts at 1.0 mOhm | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heat in the board | 4.42 W | 8.16 W | |
| R1 terminals (pins 1 / 4) | 61 / 61 C | 85 / 85 C | 107 C (PBV derating, 1.22 W, no heatsink) |
| R4 terminals (pins 1 / 4) | 66 / 66 C | 94 / 94 C | 107 C (PBV derating, 1.22 W, no heatsink) |
| R7 terminals (pins 1 / 4) | 69 / 69 C | 97 / 97 C | 107 C (PBV derating, 1.23 W, no heatsink) |
| J1 / J2 pin, phase U | 59 / 59 C | 87 / 87 C | 120 C (MR60PW) |
| J1 / J2 pin, phase V | 64 / 64 C | 95 / 95 C | 120 C (MR60PW) |
| J1 / J2 pin, phase W | 66 / 66 C | 99 / 99 C | 120 C (MR60PW) |
| IC2 (bottom, under R1) | 55 C | 74 C | |
| IC4 (bottom, under R4) | 62 C | 86 C | |
| IC6 (bottom, under R7) | 66 C | 91 C | |
| Hottest point of the board | 70 C at (3.9, -35.7) | 99 C at (15.9, -32.9) | |
| Mean of the board | 49 C | 65 C | |

Phase W runs hottest: its shunt sits 3 mm from the bottom edge of the board, with less copper around it to spread the heat. Without the contacts the hottest point is a Kelvin pin of a shunt (R7 pin 3, net OUT-3): its small pads and the Kelvin tracks of L6 take the heat that flows down from the body through the U pins, up to 8 K above the top face just there. With the contacts it is the J2 pin 1, net OUT-W.

Each cell: copper and shunts / plus the MR60PW contacts at 1.0 mOhm.
- Copper and shunts: the PBV terminals reach their derating limit at 45 A; the MR60PW pins reach 120 C beyond 50 A.
- Plus MR60PW contacts at 1.0 mOhm: the PBV terminals reach their derating limit at 37 A; the MR60PW pins reach 120 C at 40 A.

## Model

- Copper from the board file: 70 um on L1 and L6, 35 um on L2 and L3; resistivity 1.724e-8 Ohm.m at 20 C, +0.393 %/K, iterated with the temperature. Vias: 20 um barrel. Pins of J1, J2 and the shunts: one potential and one temperature over their hole on all layers.
- FR4: 0.30 W/mK through the board, 0.80 in its plane. Faces: natural convection of a horizontal plate (8.3 W/m2K up, 4.2 down at 35 A, copper and shunts) plus radiation, solder mask emissivity 0.9.
- PBV-R001: 1 mOhm, body on its four pins (copper, 0.8 mm thick, 3 mm above the board). The three bodies lose 1.41 W to the air themselves at 35 A (38 % of the shunt heat): natural convection of a vertical plate on all faces (the 5.5 mm channels between them convect nearly as freely), radiation (emissivity 0.5) only from the edges and the faces that see the room. They stand in the air the board warms, so they may lose less: with no loss from the bodies at all, the hottest PBV terminal would reach 88 C (copper and shunts) or 129 C (plus contacts) instead of 69 / 97 C. This is the largest uncertainty of the model; a thermocouple on a PBV terminal settles it. The inside is not published: 5.1 mm of terminal copper assumed from the resistive strip to each I pin (about 1 K).
- MR60PW contacts: datasheet maximum 1.0 mOhm (no typical value given); half of their heat enters the board, the other half the plug and its cable. With the cables also warming up at 35 A, the true share depends on their gauge and length.
- Not modelled: the battery line (J3, R9, J5); the cables; other parts (the analog front end is well under 1 W); the shade of the connectors and shunts on the faces; the board edges; any airflow or enclosure.

## Checks

- Heat balance: 4.4158 W in, 4.4158 W out (copper and shunts, 35 A).
- Kirchhoff: current through the shunt 35.0000 A for 35 A injected.
- validate_solver.py: ring of copper fed by a J1-size pin, resistance +2.1 % at 0.1 mm (+0.7 % at 0.05 mm), so the path resistances above lean high by about 2 %; copper sheet cooled on both faces, temperature within 0.03 % of the Bessel solution.
- Grid 0.05/0.2 mm (current / heat) instead of 0.1 / 0.2: R J1 to R1 0.1037 instead of 0.1044 mOhm, PBV R1 terminal 61.24 instead of 61.30 C, hottest point 69.57 instead of 69.64 C.
- Grid 0.1/0.4 mm (current / heat) instead of 0.1 / 0.2: R J1 to R1 0.1049 instead of 0.1044 mOhm, PBV R1 terminal 62.83 instead of 61.30 C, hottest point 71.34 instead of 69.64 C.
